title: It scorches the skin of man.
subtitle: A warning aimed at the body that sinned
then: Mujahid said this is {trap}for the skin{/trap}, and Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said it burns the skin of man. The warning is spoken to people in their bodies, the same bodies they used to walk away from the truth.
now: You moisturise, you wear sunscreen, you book the doctor when a mole looks odd. {idea}You already know your body is precious.{/idea} The verse asks you to protect it from the harm that lasts, by how you use it today.
old: My body is mine, and what I do with it is nobody's business.
new: My body is a trust, and I protect it most by using it well for Allah.
try: Use your hands today for one good deed you would normally skip, like helping carry something.

title: Over it are nineteen.
subtitle: A small number that tested big egos
then: Ibn Kathir says these are the guardians of Hell, {idea}mighty in appearance and harsh in character{/idea}. When Quraysh heard the number, Abu Jahl joked: {trap}can not every ten of you defeat one of them?{/trap}
now: Someone shares a verse in the group chat and the replies are jokes. Laughing emojis, a meme. {trap}Mockery is the easy way to avoid taking something seriously.{/trap} The verse is testing how you react, not how big the number is.
old: If something in the religion sounds strange, joking about it is harmless.
new: How I react to what I do not understand is itself the test.
try: When you meet a verse you do not understand today, look it up instead of brushing it off.

title: The same number guides some and confuses others.
subtitle: One fact, many reactions
then: Quraysh boasted they could defeat the guardians; one strongman offered to take on seventeen himself. Allah answered: {idea}none but angels{/idea}, and the number is a test. Ibn Kathir says through such examples {reward}faith becomes firm in some hearts{/reward} and {trap}shaken in others{/trap}. And none knows the soldiers of your Lord but Him.
now: Two people read the same verse on a bad day. One feels steadied. The other feels annoyed and closes the app. {idea}Same words, different hearts.{/idea} The question is never only what the verse says, but how you are holding it.
old: If a verse confuses me, the problem must be with the verse.
new: The same verse can strengthen or shake faith; what I bring to it matters.
try: Before reading Quran today, ask Allah: let this increase my faith.

title: No! By the moon.
subtitle: A firm no, then a light in the dark
then: Right after the mockery about the nineteen, Allah says {idea}No{/idea} and swears by the moon. The oath begins a series, moon, night, dawn, all leading to one statement: that the Fire is one of the great things. The jokes of Quraysh were answered with the sky.
now: You step outside late after a long shift. The moon is up over the car park. {idea}It rose without asking anyone.{/idea} The same Lord who keeps it there is the one telling you this is serious.
old: Warnings in the Quran are things I can laugh off.
new: Allah answers mockery with a firm No and an oath by His creation.
try: Look at the moon tonight for a full minute and say SubhanAllah.

title: And by the night as it turns to leave.
subtitle: Darkness does not stay
then: Ibn Kathir explains the night {idea}when it withdraws{/idea}. In Makkah, every listener knew the moment the dark starts to give way. Allah swears by that turning point, on the way to a serious statement.
now: Three in the morning in a hospital corridor, or awake with worry about rent. {idea}The night always feels like it will not end. It always does.{/idea} Every withdrawing night is a sign of a Lord in charge of change.
old: This dark time in my life is never going to end.
new: Every night turns and leaves, because Allah moves it on.
try: If you wake in the night this week, use the moment for two short units of prayer.

title: And by the dawn when it shines.
subtitle: When things become clear
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}when it shines{/reward}. After the moon and the departing night, Allah swears by the bright morning. What was hidden in darkness becomes plain to see. Next comes what all these oaths were for.
now: The first light through your blinds. You can suddenly see the mess on the floor, the face in the mirror. {idea}Dawn shows things as they are.{/idea} One day everything you did will be that visible.
old: Mornings are just the start of another rushed day.
new: Each dawn is a small sign of the Day when all things become clear.
try: Tomorrow, when you see first light, thank Allah for one more day to set things right.

title: It is one of the greatest of things.
subtitle: What the three oaths were for
then: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and others said {trap}this refers to the Hellfire{/trap}, one of the great things. The people who joked about nineteen guardians were told that what they mocked was among the gravest matters there are.
now: You treat the serious things lightly: a lie on a form, an unpaid debt, a cold silence with your mother. {idea}The verse resets the scale.{/idea} Some things are bigger than they look from your sofa.
old: The afterlife is too far away to feel like a big deal.
new: Allah calls it one of the greatest matters, so I let it shape small choices.
try: Fix one thing today you have been treating as small, like a debt or an unkept promise.

title: A warning for all humanity.
subtitle: Told in advance, out of mercy

row.title: to save
sub: told before it is too late

then: This connects to the first command of the surah: arise and warn. Here the Fire itself is {idea}a warning to mankind{/idea}. Mujahid said the description of the Fire is {reward}nothing but a reminder{/reward} for people.
now: The smoke alarm screeches at midnight. Annoying, loud, and the reason the family is alive. {reward}A warning is a gift you only resent until you need it.{/reward}
old: Talk of punishment is just meant to frighten people.
new: The warning is mercy: Allah tells me in advance so I can stay safe.
try: Thank Allah today for warning you, and change one thing because of it.

title: For whoever chooses to step forward, or hang back.
subtitle: The choice is real
then: Ibn Kathir explains it is for {reward}whoever wishes to accept the warning and be guided{/reward}, or {trap}hold back, turn away and reject it{/trap}. The warning is given to all, and each person moves.
now: The masjid is a ten minute walk. The class starts Thursday. The Quran app is on your home screen. {idea}Forward or back is a real choice you make each day.{/idea} Standing still is choosing too.
old: I will get more religious when it just happens to me.
new: Moving forward or staying behind is my choice, made in small daily steps.
try: Take one step forward today: attend, read, or call someone who helps your faith.

title: Every soul is held by what it earned.
subtitle: Deeds as a pledge
then: Ibn Abbas and others said it means {idea}bound to his deed on the Day of Judgement{/idea}. Right after the choice to go forward or stay behind, the result is stated: each soul is held as a pledge for what it did.
now: A pawnshop holds your watch until you pay. {idea}Your soul is held the same way, by what you earned.{/idea} Your parents' piety, your friends' good deeds, your surname will not pay it off for you.
old: Coming from a good family will count for me.
new: My soul is held by my own deeds, so I work on them myself.
try: Do one good deed today that is fully yours, done for no one but Allah.

title: Except the people of the right.
subtitle: The ones whose deeds set them free
then: Right after every soul is held by its deeds comes the exception: {reward}those on the Right{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says they will be in Gardens. After a long passage of warning, the door of hope appears.
now: You read the warnings and felt the weight. {reward}Here is the other side: a group whose deeds free them.{/reward} Not famous people, just people who prayed, fed others, and believed. You can be among them.
old: Paradise is for people much better than me.
new: The people of the right are ordinary believers, and the door is open to me.
try: Make dua today: O Allah, make me one of the people of the right.

title: In Gardens, asking one another.
subtitle: Safe enough to ask questions
then: Ibn Kathir describes the people of the right {reward}in lofty rooms{/reward}, in Gardens, asking each other questions. The scene is calm: they have arrived and can look back.
now: Friends sitting late after a wedding, safe, talking over how life went. {reward}That ease of conversation is a picture of Paradise.{/reward} The people you sit with now are a hint of who you will sit with then.
old: Who I spend time with now has nothing to do with my end.
new: Good company now is a preview of the company in the Gardens.
try: Spend time today with one friend who reminds you of Allah.

title: Asking about the ones who sinned.
subtitle: The question from above
then: Ibn Kathir says while they are in lofty rooms {trap}they will ask the criminals{/trap} in the lowest levels. The Quran lets us overhear this conversation now, long before it happens.
now: It is like being handed next year's exam answers, along with the list of why others failed. {idea}You get to hear the question before you are asked it.{/idea} The next verses are the answers. Read them as a checklist.
old: I cannot know what will matter on that Day.
new: The Quran lets me overhear that Day's conversation, so I can prepare now.
try: Read verses 42 to 47 of this surah today and pick one point to work on.

title: What brought you into Saqar?
subtitle: The question that sums up a life
then: The question is {idea}What has caused you to enter Saqar?{/idea} The word means what led you, what path you walked. It assumes there was a road, made of choices. The answers follow in the next verses.
now: Your friend asks how you ended up in debt, or burnt out, or far from your family. {idea}You can usually trace it back to a few habits.{/idea} Better to ask yourself that question now, gently, while the road can still change.
old: Where I end up is mostly down to luck.
new: Every end has a path, and I can ask today where mine is leading.
try: Ask yourself tonight: what habit of mine is leading me somewhere I do not want to go?
